title.rendered: Moved by the Impulses of the Spirit: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: The mature children of God are moved by the impulses of the Holy Spirit. Being led by the Spirit is the everyday inheritance of every son and daughter in Christ.

content.rendered:
The mature children of God are moved by the impulses of the Holy Spirit. Being led by the Spirit is not reserved for a few spiritual elites. It is the everyday inheritance of every son and every daughter of God in Christ.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, May 25, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“The mature children of God are those who are moved by the impulses of the Holy Spirit.”
Romans 8:14 (TPT)

Today’s Message

Yesterday was Pentecost Sunday. The day the Spirit was poured out. But Pentecost is not the destination. It is the doorway. The disciples did not stay in the upper room after the fire fell. They walked out into Jerusalem changed people, and from that day forward their lives were ordered by something they had never known before—the leading of an indwelling Spirit.

The Passion Translation renders Romans 8:14 with a striking phrase. The mature children of God are those who are moved by the impulses of the Holy Spirit. Not the impulses of fear. Not the impulses of self-protection. Not the impulses of the crowd. The impulses of the Spirit who is in them.

This is the daily reality of Pentecost. The Spirit who fell on the disciples now lives in every believer, and He is not silent. He nudges. He prompts. He gently turns. He whispers a word into a conversation, a thought into a decision, a check into a moment, a peace into a confusion. The Christian life is not a list of rules to follow. It is a Person to follow, dwelling inside you.

And notice the word Paul uses for those who walk this way: the children of God. Not the slaves. Not the employees. Not the volunteers. Children. Sons and daughters. In the next verse Paul will say it explicitly: “You have not received a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear. You have received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry ‘Abba, Father.’” The Spirit who leads you is not a taskmaster. He is the Spirit of a Father whose love for you was settled before time began.

So this morning, the question is not whether you are doing enough to qualify for His leading. You are already a son. You are already a daughter. You already have the Spirit. The question is whether you are tender to His impulses. Are you listening? Are you slowing down enough to feel the gentle pressure of His leading? Are you trusting that the impulse you sensed yesterday and dismissed was really Him?

Walking by the Spirit is not complicated. It is a relationship with a Helper who is in you, for you, and never against you. Today, lean into His leading. Notice the nudges. Trust the Father’s heart behind them. You are not figuring this out alone. The Spirit who fell at Pentecost is the Spirit who walks you through this Monday.

Prayer

Father, thank You that I am Your son, that I am Your daughter, that the Spirit of adoption lives in me. Make me tender today to the impulses of Your Spirit. Slow me down when I need to slow down. Move me when I need to move. Speak gently and clearly, and give me ears to hear and a heart to follow. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am a son. I am a daughter. The Spirit of God lives in me, and He leads me as a child of the Father, not as a slave. Today I walk by His impulses, not by the impulses of fear. I am led, I am loved, I am held.
